clue.text: Dog collar put back, then put away

indicators.note: put back tells us to turn the dog-and-collar pair end to end, reading them right to left

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog
to collar someone is to nab or arrest them

explanation.surface: Someone fastens a dog's collar, then tidies it away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses the whole run PUGNAB, giving BAN + GUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang idiom: to bang someone up is to lock them in prison, i.e. put them away.

clue.text: Open a drink

parts.note: a jar is British slang for a glass of beer

explanation.surface: An invitation to crack open a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left slightly open is said to be ajar.

clue.text: Ride high where observation was out of this world

definitions.text: where observation was out of this world

parts.note: to go on a fairground ride is to ride it
hilly country is high ground

explanation.surface: A rider climbs to a lofty spot with an unearthly view.
explanation.walkthrough: GOONHILLY Downs in Cornwall housed a famous satellite earth station, observing and communicating with space.
explanation.definitionFit: Location: the Cornish satellite tracking station watched and talked to spacecraft, so its observation was literally beyond Earth.

clue.text: Aussie native takes vessel with uranium to inject into sporting rival?

indicators.note: to inject into means the vessel and uranium go inside the word for the rival

parts.note: Pom is Australian slang for an English person, the old rival at cricket and rugby
SS is the abbreviation for steamship
U is the chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: An Australian creature carries a radioactive ship towards an English opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: POM is Australian slang for a Briton, England being Australia's great sporting rival.
explanation.definitionFit: The possum is a marsupial native to Australia, an example of its wildlife.

clue.text: A revolutionary leader abandons persuading revolutionary to get enlisted

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned over, so the remaining letters are rearranged
abandons means the named letters are dropped out of the word persuading
the leader of a word is its first letter, here the start of revolutionary

explanation.surface: A rebel abandons the effort to persuade a fellow radical to join up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandons' removes R (the leader of 'revolutionary') and A from PERSUADING, leaving PESUDING, which the second 'revolutionary' shuffles.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal synonym: having signed up for the forces is having enlisted.

clue.text: Bound to claim rapids safer, perhaps, where Aussies on the water

indicators.note: to claim means the outer word takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: bound in the sense 'certain to' means sure

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of rapids safer are not in their final order

explanation.surface: Something is certain to make river rapids safer for Australians boating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the letters of 'rapids safer'. SURFERS PARADISE is a beach resort on Queensland's Gold Coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Place name: the Gold Coast resort is famed for Australians riding the surf.

clue.text: Wanders about British home for "The Lion King" by George

indicators.note: about means the word for wanders goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to gad about is to wander in search of fun
a lion in Britain lives in a zoo
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A trip round Britain for the musical The Lion King, written by George.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Lion King' looks like the musical; split it: the lion's home is ZOO, King is K.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dated exclamations of surprise, oaths of mild astonishment.

clue.text: Bird eaten up by poltergeist

indicators.note: up, in a down clue, means the letters read from bottom to top
eaten by means the bird is swallowed inside the word poltergeist

explanation.surface: A bird is devoured by a mischievous ghost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eaten' finds TERGE inside poltERGEist; 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: The egret is a white heron, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Kid returns fitted garment

indicators.note: fitted suggests the letters are tailored into a new shape

explanation.surface: A child brings back a tailored item of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: An underskirt is a petticoat, a type of clothing worn beneath a skirt.

clue.text: One taking drink-driver round roundabout

indicators.note: round means the word for driver encircles the roundabout shape

parts.note: a driver is a car user
a roundabout is circular, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: A drink-driver is arrested going round a traffic roundabout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roundabout' tempts as the definition, pointing to CAROUSEL; it only supplies the round letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone carousing drinks merrily and noisily.

clue.text: Have a go at getting clear in river

indicators.note: in places the word for clear inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales
to rid a place of something is to clear it

explanation.surface: Someone tries clearing out a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to have a go at someone is to criticise or mock them.

clue.text: Transferring teacher to university tripled the best habits

indicators.note: transferring indicates the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for university, taken three times

explanation.surface: A teacher moves to university, where results tripled.
explanation.definitionFit: Habits means clothing, and top-end designer fashion is the finest clothing.

clue.text: Comedian in charge upset member, which stinks!

indicators.note: in puts the comedian inside the charge word
upset in a down clue means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: a charge for a service is a fee; plural fees
a wag is a joker or wit
an arm is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: A comic in charge of a member gets upset by a terrible smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses the charge word, which is then split by the comedian; 'member' is a limb here, not a club member.
explanation.definitionFit: A sewage farm processes waste, so it is a place that smells foul.

clue.text: See 18
Drop axes name, or (heavens!) name on chopper

indicators.note: axes means cuts out, so the letter for name is chopped from the word for drop

parts.note: to sink is to drop down
the sky is the heavens

explanation.surface: Someone drops the axe on a name in alarm, writing it on a chopper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'axes' removes N (name) from SINK, leaving SIK.
explanation.definitionFit: Brand name: Sikorsky is a famous maker of helicopters, a name seen on many.

clue.text: Where Jordan's inclined, say, to have row about one part of speech

indicators.note: about means the word for row surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a rank is a row, as of soldiers
I is the Roman numeral one
a verb is one of the grammatical parts of speech

explanation.surface: A celebrity named Jordan is inclined to argue about grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: Jordan is the river; its sloping side is a bank. 'say' marks this as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The bank of a river slopes up, so the Jordan's inclined edge is an example.

clue.text: Girl, one not fat like a great Italian

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
I is the Roman numeral for one
lean means slim, not fat

explanation.surface: A slender girl resembling an Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective formed from Galileo, the great Italian astronomer, meaning relating to him.

clue.text: Huge rodent film director Frank captures by rotating camera, ultimately

indicators.note: captures means the director's name surrounds the other letters

parts.note: Frank Capra directed It's a Wonderful Life

indicators.note: rotating turns the little word by around
ultimately points to the final letter of camera

explanation.surface: A film director captures a giant rodent by turning the camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotating' turns 'by' round; 'ultimately' takes the last letter of 'camera'; both go inside the director's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: The capybara of South America is the largest living rodent.

clue.text: With regret superbly

definitions.meaning: said reluctantly, a grudging 'all right then' to accept something

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a reluctant assent and an adverb meaning extremely good.

clue.text: In a book, gas inhaled

indicators.note: inhaled means the gas is drawn inside the word for book

parts.note: a tome is a large book
H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen, a gas

explanation.surface: Breathing in gas while reading a book.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in means being home, not out; a synonymous phrase.

clue.text: Very old killer, Irish, held by kidnapper alongside love, frantic

indicators.note: frantic means wildly agitated, so the letters of love are jumbled
held by means the Irish abbreviation sits inside the word for kidnapper

parts.note: a captor holds someone captive

explanation.surface: An elderly Irish murderer is held by a frantic, lovesick kidnapper.
explanation.definitionFit: The velociraptor was a predatory dinosaur, a killer from millions of years ago.

clue.text: Classic car, which won't start, stops here

indicators.note: which won't start means the first letter of the car's name is lost

parts.note: the Morgan is a classic British sports car

explanation.surface: A vintage car that won't start comes to a halt here.
explanation.walkthrough: An organ has stops, knobs that select sets of pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: Pipe organs have stops, the controls that switch ranks of pipes on and off.

clue.text: Wooden smile?

definitions.meaning: a timber, a long piece of wood used in building

explanation.definitionFit: A beam is a timber, and to beam is to smile radiantly.

clue.text: Engineer's western view

parts.note: an angle is a point of view

explanation.surface: An engineer has a western perspective.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to engineer an outcome by cunning is to fix or arrange it.

clue.text: Alone, one dead in the ground

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in puts the word for dead inside the word for the ground

parts.note: sod is turf, the soil of the ground
the late person is one who has died

explanation.surface: Alone, a person lies dead in the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on one's own and cut off from others is being isolated.

clue.text: Source of gold in money, no capital for bank

indicators.note: in means the gold source sits inside the shortened money word
no capital means the first letter of the money word is removed

parts.note: pence are coins, small change
a gold mine is where gold comes from

explanation.surface: A gold source among the cash, but the bank has no capital.
explanation.definitionFit: An eminence is a rise of ground, and a bank is a raised slope.

clue.text: Go on the piste in March, heading off — my home's a cold climate

indicators.note: in places the skiing word inside the shortened march word
heading off removes the first letter of the march word

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
to ski is to go on the piste, a ski run

explanation.surface: Skiing in March with the head turned away; my home is very cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'March' looks like the month; it is DEMO, a protest march, losing D.
explanation.definitionFit: Arctic people traditionally lived in a cold climate; the word is now often considered offensive.
